## Episode Thesis

Former Riksbank governor Stefan Ingves discusses a busy week of central bank rate decisions, the US economy (high budget deficits, rising national debt, Trump's policies slowing growth), and the oil-price shock from the Hormuz Strait closure as a new inflation risk. He defends the 2% inflation target, repeats his case for Sweden joining the euro, and discusses central bank gold buying. He also flags household debt tied to a dysfunctional housing market and the ever-present risk of banking crises. The discussion is macro-focused with a cautious tone, and no stock-specific investment views are given.
